label: copy phase: re-input of r (and g/b/l later in the copy)
explanation: Reset-gate unit that is almost only active in the copy phase (98% of mass); it is never active at the delimiter, and the only original-phase activity is at t=0 (2% of mass, mostly when the first token is r). Activity depends on which token is being fed back in: r is by far the strongest (47% active rate, 46% of mass, includes every top example near max), then g, b and l, with weaker contributions from z and w. The firing rate also rises with copy position (recall_idx 0 never fires, 1 rarely; peaks at recall_idx 3-4 and the last steps of long sequences), and longer sequences fire more. Predicate: copy-phase input r, or g/b/l at recall_idx>=2. Dev F1 0.59, mass recall 0.78. About 22% of mass falls on weak activations to other copy-phase tokens (o, z, w, f, 3, ...), and many g/b/l inputs do not fire, so it is token-weighted and position-graded rather than a clean token detector.
